# Tech Faculty NG

> Tech Faculty NG trains, certifies and places Nigerians in tech careers: 10 departments online or at 22 campuses across Nigeria, a Free AI Course (Everyday AI & Digital Productivity) with a free Certificate of Completion, SIWES industrial training placements, 107 pay-per-task services for businesses and the matching 107 paid side hustles for talent, and a jobs and talent marketplace. Licensed by the Federal Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation (FMSTI) through the National Board for Technology Incubation (NBTI).

Short version with links: https://techfaculty.ng/llms.txt

## Key facts

- Tech Faculty NG is a Nigerian technology training institute. Licensed by the Federal Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation (FMSTI) through the National Board for Technology Incubation (NBTI).
- Headquarters: Technology Incubation Center, Onitsha-Okigwe Expressway, by Area Command, Umudim, Nnewi, Anambra State.
- Campuses: 22 centres in 19 states and the FCT (Nnewi, Awka, Onitsha, Owerri, Aba, Enugu, Abakaliki, Abuja, Lagos, Ibadan, Port Harcourt, Benin City, Kaduna, Kano, Jos, Bauchi, Makurdi, Uyo, Calabar, Sokoto, Ilorin, Akure). 20 of them operate inside NBTI Technology Incubation Centres.
- Departments: Web Development, Mobile App Development, Data Science & Analytics, Cybersecurity, AI & Machine Learning, Basic Internet & AI Studies, Social Media & Digital Marketing, Design, Cloud Computing, Robotics & IoT.
- Every department can be studied online, hybrid or in person.
- Free starting point: Basic Internet & AI Studies (3 weeks), no fee.
- Paid programmes are priced per module in naira and shown in US dollars outside Nigeria. Learning mode adds to the module total: online only is included, hybrid mode +₦12,000, physical classes +₦22,500.
- On-site SIWES at any campus: no separate placement fee. Learn & Pay students pay the regular course fee for their department, with up to 50% off for SIWES and IT students on request; Tutor & Earn students are paid. Virtual SIWES is charged because it covers courier delivery.
- Virtual SIWES (online industrial training placement): ₦45,000. Logbook review, signing, stamping and two-way courier delivery: ₦15,000.
- SIWES Success Kit: ₦4,500.
- Pay-per-task services for businesses: 107 fixed-price tasks in 8 categories (Content & Creative, Marketing & Social Media, Field Sales & Reps, Web & Development, Testing & QA, Cybersecurity, AI & Automation, Admin & Virtual Assistance), from ₦7,500 per task at https://techfaculty.ng/services. Standard orders can be paid online immediately; custom or bulk work gets a quote with a pay link. No salary, no contract.
- Side hustles for talent: the same 107 tasks are paid work for Nigerians at https://techfaculty.ng/side-hustles: ₦5,000 per standard task or ₦10,000 per big task, paid weekly every Friday for approved tasks, 50 openings per side hustle. Joining the talent pool is free.
- Jobs and talent marketplace at https://techfaculty.ng/careers: Tech Faculty roles and client projects (apply with one free talent profile), plus curated remote tech and AI-training jobs open to Nigerians from partner platforms (Micro1, Ask Ethos, Atlas Capture, Mercor, Outlier, Handshake AI, Alignerr, Toloka, Turing), refreshed twice a month.
- Hiring: businesses can browse the public talent pool at https://techfaculty.ng/talent/pool or send a brief at https://techfaculty.ng/hire. A Vetted badge means the person passed a Tech Faculty assessment or work trial, or is a Tech Faculty student or graduate.
- Studying from outside Nigeria: every programme can be taken online from any country, with prices shown and charged in US dollars (₦1,400 = $1); details at https://techfaculty.ng/study-online-africa.
- Certificates: each graduate gets one Certificate of Achievement, issued from the student dashboard and verifiable by Faculty ID or certificate number at https://techfaculty.ng/verify.
- Software products: Tech Faculty also builds and publishes its own apps (Dear Claire, Alter Ego, Eavesdrop, AI Clopedia, Pet Care Card, ExamsAi.ng, SkillFlow, UnilagLife, Baby Care Cards, Plant Care Cards, AutoPR by PR Faculty), listed at https://techfaculty.ng/products.
- AI assistants can query live programmes, services, side hustles, open roles, jobs and the public talent pool through the public Tech Faculty MCP server (no sign-in needed): https://flxwtwzjslufglpwfjdx.supabase.co/functions/v1/mcp
- Google rating for the Nnewi campus: 4.9 from 90 reviews (checked October 2026), https://www.google.com/maps/place/?q=place_id:ChIJ5ZxSzmi9QxAR23OzR7YbAkM.
- Contact: WhatsApp +2348068597140, email thetechfaculty@gmail.com.

## Programme prices

Paid programmes are priced per module. Students choose the modules they want, a learning mode and optional add-ons; the order must reach the plan's minimum.

- Online Only: included (Self-paced learning with recorded lectures).
- Hybrid Mode: +₦12,000 (Online + Monthly physical meetups).
- Physical Classes: +₦22,500 (Weekly on-site classes).

- Web Development: 6 modules totalling ₦82,500 online. Students pay per module, and an order (modules, learning mode and add-ons) starts at ₦50,000.
- Mobile App Development: 6 modules totalling ₦105,000 online. Students pay per module, and an order (modules, learning mode and add-ons) starts at ₦80,000.
- Data Science & Analytics: 6 modules totalling ₦82,500 online. Students pay per module, and an order (modules, learning mode and add-ons) starts at ₦100,000.
- Cybersecurity: 6 modules totalling ₦100,500 online. Students pay per module, and an order (modules, learning mode and add-ons) starts at ₦120,000.
- AI & Machine Learning: 6 modules totalling ₦124,500 online. Students pay per module, and an order (modules, learning mode and add-ons) starts at ₦150,000.
- Basic Internet & AI Studies: Free.
- Social Media & Digital Marketing: 6 modules totalling ₦72,000 online. Students pay per module, and an order (modules, learning mode and add-ons) starts at ₦60,000.
- Design: 6 modules totalling ₦78,000 online. Students pay per module, and an order (modules, learning mode and add-ons) starts at ₦70,000.
- Cloud Computing: 6 modules totalling ₦103,500 online. Students pay per module, and an order (modules, learning mode and add-ons) starts at ₦130,000.
- Robotics & IoT: Taken as a Custom Programme: students pick modules from any department, and an order starts at ₦50,000.

## Departments

### Web Development

Page: https://techfaculty.ng/departments/web-development
Duration: 12-16 weeks. Level: Beginner to Advanced.
Price: 6 modules totalling ₦82,500 online. Students pay per module, and an order (modules, learning mode and add-ons) starts at ₦50,000.
Modules: HTML/CSS Fundamentals ₦7,500; JavaScript Mastery ₦12,000; React Development ₦18,000; Node.js & Backend ₦18,000; Database Management ₦12,000; Full-Stack Projects ₦15,000.
Optional add-ons: Job Placement Support ₦15,000; Internship Access ₦12,000; Mentor Network Access ₦18,000; Industry Certification Prep ₦22,500; Tech Faculty Certificate free.

Web development is still the fastest route from beginner to paid work in Nigeria, and in 2026 the bar has moved: employers expect you to ship real apps and use AI tools well. Our Web Development department takes you from your first HTML page to deployed full-stack React applications, with weekly code reviews, portfolio projects, and a hiring-focused final capstone. Study online from anywhere or in person at any Tech Faculty centre inside a Technology Incubation Centre.

Curriculum: HTML, CSS & Responsive Layouts; JavaScript & TypeScript Fundamentals; React & Next.js; Node.js, Express & REST APIs; Databases, Auth & Deployment; AI-Assisted Development Workflows; Capstone: Ship a Production App.
Tools: React, Next.js, TypeScript, Node.js, Tailwind CSS, Git & GitHub, Supabase, Vercel.
Who it is for: Complete beginners who want a first tech skill; Students and NYSC members building a portfolio; Designers moving into front-end engineering; Business owners who want to build their own products.
Career outcomes (Nigerian salary bands): Junior Front-End Developer ₦250,000 – ₦450,000 / month; Full-Stack Developer ₦500,000 – ₦1,200,000 / month; Remote Contract Developer $1,500 – $4,000 / month.

Q: Do I need a laptop to join the Web Development department?
A: Yes. A laptop with at least 8GB RAM is recommended, because you will run a code editor, a browser and a local server together. Our tech store sells tested student laptops with three months of hardware support, and on-campus students can use centre workstations during class hours.

Q: Will I get a certificate?
A: Yes. Every Web Development graduate who completes the projects and the capstone receives a Tech Faculty NG certificate. Each certificate carries its own ID that employers, schools and clients can check on our public verification portal, so nobody has to take a PDF on trust.

### Mobile App Development

Page: https://techfaculty.ng/departments/mobile-app-development
Duration: 14-18 weeks. Level: Intermediate.
Price: 6 modules totalling ₦105,000 online. Students pay per module, and an order (modules, learning mode and add-ons) starts at ₦80,000.
Modules: React Native Development ₦18,000; Flutter & Dart ₦18,000; iOS with Swift ₦21,000; Android with Kotlin ₦21,000; Mobile UI/UX Design ₦12,000; Cross-Platform Projects ₦15,000.
Optional add-ons: Job Placement Support ₦15,000; Internship Access ₦12,000; Mentor Network Access ₦18,000; Industry Certification Prep ₦22,500; Tech Faculty Certificate free.

Nigeria is a mobile-first market, and the developers who can ship a working app to Google Play or the App Store are the ones who get hired and get clients. This department takes you through cross-platform development with React Native and Flutter, native basics in Swift and Kotlin, offline-first patterns for poor networks, payments, push notifications, and the full store-submission process. You graduate with at least one published app under your own name.

Curriculum: Mobile UI Fundamentals & Design Systems; React Native & Expo; Flutter & Dart; iOS Development with Swift (Foundations); Android Development with Kotlin (Foundations); Payments, Push Notifications & Offline Sync; App Store & Google Play Publishing.
Tools: React Native, Expo, Flutter, Dart, Swift, Kotlin, Firebase, Figma.
Who it is for: Web developers adding mobile to their stack; Founders who want to launch their own app; Students targeting product engineering roles; Freelancers serving Nigerian SMEs.
Career outcomes (Nigerian salary bands): Junior Mobile Developer ₦300,000 – ₦500,000 / month; Senior Mobile Engineer ₦700,000 – ₦1,500,000 / month; Freelance App Builder ₦400,000 – ₦2,000,000 per project.

Q: Can I build iPhone apps without a Mac?
A: Yes, for learning and testing. We use Expo's cloud build service, so students on Windows laptops can produce iOS builds without owning a Mac. A Mac only becomes necessary for advanced native Swift work, which comes late in the 14 to 18 week Mobile App Development programme.

Q: Do you help with publishing to the stores?
A: Yes. Publishing is part of the final module. We cover the store listing, screenshots, the Apple and Google review guidelines and the submission itself, so your capstone app goes through the real Google Play and App Store submission process instead of staying on your laptop.

### Data Science & Analytics

Page: https://techfaculty.ng/departments/data-science-analytics
Duration: 12-16 weeks. Level: Beginner to Advanced.
Price: 6 modules totalling ₦82,500 online. Students pay per module, and an order (modules, learning mode and add-ons) starts at ₦100,000.
Modules: Python Programming ₦10,500; SQL & Databases ₦9,000; Data Visualization ₦12,000; Statistical Analysis ₦13,500; Machine Learning Basics ₦22,500; Real-world Data Projects ₦15,000.
Optional add-ons: Job Placement Support ₦15,000; Internship Access ₦12,000; Mentor Network Access ₦18,000; One-on-One Mentorship (1hr/week) ₦30,000; Tech Faculty Certificate free.

Every Nigerian bank, hospital, retailer and government agency now collects more data than it can read. Our Data Science & Analytics department trains you to close that gap: clean messy spreadsheets, query databases with SQL, build executive dashboards in Power BI, and run predictive models in Python. Every module ends with a portfolio deliverable built on real Nigerian data — NBS, CBN, open health and commerce datasets — so your work looks like the job before you have the job.

Curriculum: Excel for Analysts & Data Cleaning; SQL & Database Management; Data Visualisation with Power BI; Tableau & Looker Studio; Python for Data Analysis (pandas, NumPy); Statistics & Experiment Design; Machine Learning Fundamentals; Capstone: End-to-End Analytics Project.
Tools: Excel, SQL, Power BI, Tableau, Looker Studio, Python, pandas, scikit-learn.
Who it is for: Graduates switching from non-tech backgrounds; Accountants, auditors and operations staff; Business owners who want data-led decisions; Students targeting analyst and BI roles.
Career outcomes (Nigerian salary bands): Junior Data Analyst ₦250,000 – ₦450,000 / month; Business Intelligence Analyst ₦500,000 – ₦900,000 / month; Data Scientist ₦800,000 – ₦2,000,000 / month.

Q: Do I need to be good at mathematics?
A: No. Secondary-school mathematics is enough to start the Data Science & Analytics programme. We teach the statistics you need module by module over 12 to 16 weeks, applied to real Nigerian datasets rather than as theory, so you learn each method by answering a business question with it.

Q: Is Power BI or Tableau better for jobs in Nigeria?
A: Power BI, for most job seekers in Nigeria. It appears in far more Nigerian job adverts because so many companies already run Microsoft 365. We teach Power BI first, then Tableau and Looker Studio, so you can work in whichever tool an employer uses and show a dashboard built in each.

### Cybersecurity

Page: https://techfaculty.ng/departments/cybersecurity
Duration: 16-20 weeks. Level: Intermediate to Advanced.
Price: 6 modules totalling ₦100,500 online. Students pay per module, and an order (modules, learning mode and add-ons) starts at ₦120,000.
Modules: Network Security ₦15,000; Ethical Hacking ₦22,500; SOC Operations ₦18,000; Incident Response ₦12,000; CompTIA Prep ₦15,000; CEH Prep ₦18,000.
Optional add-ons: Job Placement Support ₦15,000; Internship Access ₦12,000; Mentor Network Access ₦18,000; Industry Certification Prep ₦22,500; Tech Faculty Certificate free.

Nigerian fintechs, banks and public agencies are hiring defenders faster than schools can produce them, and NDPR enforcement has made compliance skills billable. This department builds you into a job-ready analyst: networking and operating-system fundamentals first, then hands-on labs in threat detection, ethical hacking, digital forensics and incident response, plus structured preparation for CompTIA Security+ and CEH. You finish with a documented lab portfolio and an incident-response runbook you wrote yourself.

Curriculum: Networking & Operating System Security; Threat Landscape & Security Operations (SOC); Ethical Hacking & Penetration Testing; Digital Forensics & Incident Response; Cloud & Application Security; NDPR, ISO 27001 & Compliance; Certification Prep (CompTIA Security+, CEH).
Tools: Kali Linux, Wireshark, Burp Suite, Splunk, Nmap, Metasploit, Microsoft Defender.
Who it is for: IT support staff moving into security; Computer science and engineering graduates; Compliance and risk officers in fintech; Career switchers targeting remote SOC roles.
Career outcomes (Nigerian salary bands): SOC Analyst (Tier 1) ₦350,000 – ₦600,000 / month; Penetration Tester ₦700,000 – ₦1,500,000 / month; Security / GRC Consultant ₦900,000 – ₦2,500,000 / month.

Q: Do I need a computer science degree?
A: No. Most of our cybersecurity graduates come from other disciplines. What matters is completing the hands-on labs in the 16 to 20 week programme and explaining your findings clearly in writing. Employers hiring for security operations roles care more about what you can do and document than about your degree.

Q: Are certification exam fees included?
A: No. Training and exam preparation for CompTIA Security+ and CEH are included in your programme fee. The vendor exam fee itself is paid directly to CompTIA or EC-Council when you book and sit the exam, so you only pay it once you are ready to pass.

### AI & Machine Learning

Page: https://techfaculty.ng/departments/ai-machine-learning
Duration: 16-20 weeks. Level: Advanced.
Price: 6 modules totalling ₦124,500 online. Students pay per module, and an order (modules, learning mode and add-ons) starts at ₦150,000.
Modules: Deep Learning ₦27,000; Neural Networks ₦22,500; TensorFlow/PyTorch ₦18,000; NLP Fundamentals ₦21,000; Computer Vision ₦21,000; AI Deployment ₦15,000.
Optional add-ons: Job Placement Support ₦15,000; Internship Access ₦12,000; Mentor Network Access ₦18,000; One-on-One Mentorship (1hr/week) ₦30,000; VIP Classes at Chosen Location ₦75,000; Tech Faculty Certificate free.

AI is the centre of gravity for everything we teach. This department moves you from Python foundations to deployed intelligent systems: classical machine learning, deep learning with PyTorch, and the generative stack Nigerian companies are actually buying — retrieval-augmented generation, agent workflows, evaluation and cost control. You build three portfolio systems, including a WhatsApp AI agent for a Nigerian business, and learn to deploy them affordably on modest infrastructure.

Curriculum: Python & Mathematics for AI; Classical Machine Learning; Deep Learning with PyTorch & TensorFlow; Natural Language Processing; Computer Vision; Generative AI, RAG & Vector Databases; AI Agents & Automation; Model Deployment, Evaluation & Cost Control.
Tools: Python, PyTorch, TensorFlow, Hugging Face, LangChain, pgvector, FastAPI, Docker.
Who it is for: Developers adding AI to their skill set; Data analysts moving into machine learning; Founders building AI products; Researchers and postgraduate students.
Career outcomes (Nigerian salary bands): Machine Learning Engineer ₦700,000 – ₦1,800,000 / month; AI Application Developer ₦500,000 – ₦1,200,000 / month; Remote AI Trainer / Evaluator $15 – $60 / hour.

Q: Do I need a powerful computer or GPU?
A: No. We run heavy model training in Google Colab and other cloud notebooks, so any laptop with a stable browser and internet connection is enough for the AI & Machine Learning programme. An older laptop or a power cut will not stop your training jobs, because they run in the cloud.

Q: Can this lead to remote AI work?
A: Yes. Many AI & Machine Learning graduates start on AI training and evaluation platforms while they build their own projects, then move into engineering roles. Live remote and Nigerian AI roles are listed on our jobs board, and graduates can join the Tech Faculty talent pool that employers hire from.

### Basic Internet & AI Studies

Page: https://techfaculty.ng/departments/basic-internet-ai-studies
Duration: 3 weeks. Level: Beginner.
Price: Free.

You do not need to become a programmer to benefit from AI. This department is for adults, traders, civil servants, teachers and students who want confidence with a computer and real productivity with AI tools. In three weeks you learn the internet safely, handle email and documents, use ChatGPT and other assistants for writing, research and business tasks, and protect yourself from the scams that follow every new technology.

Curriculum: Computer & Internet Basics; Email, Documents & Microsoft Office; AI Tools for Everyday Work; ChatGPT & AI Assistants for Business; Online Safety, Privacy & Scam Awareness; Digital Communication & Social Presence.
Tools: Windows, Google Workspace, Microsoft Office, ChatGPT, Gemini, Canva.
Who it is for: Adults new to computers; Traders and small business owners; Teachers and civil servants; Parents and retirees getting online.
Career outcomes (Nigerian salary bands): Confident everyday computer user Foundation for any tech track; AI-assisted admin & office support ₦120,000 – ₦300,000 / month; Small business owner using AI daily Direct time and cost savings.

Q: I have never used a computer. Can I still join?
A: Yes. Basic Internet & AI Studies is built for people who have never used a computer. We start from switching the machine on, then move through the internet, email, documents and everyday AI tools like ChatGPT. Classes are short, run online or at any of our centres, and the programme is free.

### Social Media & Digital Marketing

Page: https://techfaculty.ng/departments/digital-marketing
Duration: 10-14 weeks. Level: Beginner to Intermediate.
Price: 6 modules totalling ₦72,000 online. Students pay per module, and an order (modules, learning mode and add-ons) starts at ₦60,000.
Modules: Social Media Strategy ₦10,500; Content Marketing ₦12,000; SEO/SEM ₦15,000; Video Editing ₦13,500; Photo Editing ₦9,000; Analytics & Growth ₦12,000.
Optional add-ons: Job Placement Support ₦15,000; Internship Access ₦12,000; Mentor Network Access ₦18,000; Tech Faculty Certificate free.

Marketing is the skill that pays for itself fastest, because the first client can be your own business. This department covers the full modern stack: content strategy and short-form video, SEO that survives AI search, Meta and Google advertising with real budgets, email and WhatsApp marketing, analytics, and the AI tools that now do the heavy lifting on copy, design and reporting. Every learner runs a live campaign for a real Nigerian brand before graduating.

Curriculum: Marketing Strategy & Brand Positioning; Content Creation & Short-Form Video; Photography, Editing & Graphic Basics; SEO & AI Search Visibility; Meta, Google & TikTok Advertising; Email & WhatsApp Marketing; AI Tools for Marketers; Analytics, Reporting & Growth.
Tools: Meta Ads Manager, Google Ads, Google Analytics, Canva, CapCut, Mailchimp, ChatGPT.
Who it is for: Business owners marketing their own brand; Aspiring social media managers; Content creators monetising an audience; Corporate staff moving into marketing.
Career outcomes (Nigerian salary bands): Social Media Manager ₦200,000 – ₦450,000 / month; Performance Marketer ₦400,000 – ₦900,000 / month; Freelance Marketing Consultant ₦150,000 – ₦600,000 per client.

Q: Do I need an ad budget to learn paid advertising?
A: No, you can start without one. We run shared classroom campaigns on Meta Ads Manager and Google Ads, so you practise on live data before spending your own money. A small personal test budget helps once you run your own ads, and you learn to keep that spending small and measurable.

Q: Is this useful for my existing business?
A: Yes. Many participants join the Social Media & Digital Marketing programme specifically to market their own shop, school or service, and recover the fee from new customers within the 10 to 14 weeks. The campaigns, content and analytics you build in class are ones you can keep running afterwards.

### Design

Page: https://techfaculty.ng/departments/design
Duration: 12-16 weeks. Level: Beginner to Advanced.
Price: 6 modules totalling ₦78,000 online. Students pay per module, and an order (modules, learning mode and add-ons) starts at ₦70,000.
Modules: Design Principles ₦9,000; Figma Mastery ₦12,000; Adobe Suite ₦15,000; Product Design ₦18,000; Design Systems ₦13,500; Portfolio Projects ₦10,500.
Optional add-ons: Job Placement Support ₦15,000; Internship Access ₦12,000; Mentor Network Access ₦18,000; Tech Faculty Certificate free.

Good design is why one product gets used and an identical one gets ignored. This department trains both sides of the craft: visual design for brand, print and social, and product design for interfaces people actually complete tasks in. You learn typography, colour and layout properly, then move into Figma, design systems, prototyping and usability testing, finishing with a portfolio of three case studies written the way hiring managers and clients read them.

Curriculum: Design Fundamentals: Typography, Colour & Layout; Graphic Design with Adobe Photoshop & Illustrator; Brand Identity & Print Design; UI Design with Figma; UX Research, Wireframing & Usability Testing; Design Systems & Prototyping; Portfolio & Case Study Writing.
Tools: Figma, Adobe Photoshop, Adobe Illustrator, Canva, Framer, Notion.
Who it is for: Creatives turning talent into a career; Developers who want to design their own products; Marketers producing their own assets; Freelancers raising their rates.
Career outcomes (Nigerian salary bands): Junior Graphic Designer ₦180,000 – ₦400,000 / month; Product / UI Designer ₦450,000 – ₦1,100,000 / month; Freelance Designer ₦100,000 – ₦800,000 per project.

Q: Do I need to be good at drawing?
A: No. Digital design is about hierarchy, spacing, colour and clarity, and those are skills you learn by practice rather than talent for drawing. Drawing is a bonus in the Design department, not a requirement. Most of the work happens in Figma and Adobe tools, where layout matters far more than illustration.

Q: Which software will I use?
A: Figma for app and website interfaces, Adobe Photoshop and Illustrator for visual and print work, and Canva for fast turnaround on social media graphics. You also meet Framer and Notion, and you finish the 12 to 16 week Design programme with portfolio projects made in these tools.

### Cloud Computing

Page: https://techfaculty.ng/departments/cloud-computing
Duration: 14-18 weeks. Level: Intermediate to Advanced.
Price: 6 modules totalling ₦103,500 online. Students pay per module, and an order (modules, learning mode and add-ons) starts at ₦130,000.
Modules: AWS Fundamentals ₦18,000; Azure Basics ₦18,000; GCP Essentials ₦18,000; Kubernetes & Docker ₦22,500; CI/CD Pipelines ₦15,000; Cloud Certifications ₦12,000.
Optional add-ons: Job Placement Support ₦15,000; Internship Access ₦12,000; Mentor Network Access ₦18,000; Industry Certification Prep ₦22,500; Tech Faculty Certificate free.

Cloud and DevOps skills carry some of the highest salaries in Nigerian tech and travel well into remote contracts. This department is lab-heavy from day one: you provision real infrastructure, containerise applications, build CI/CD pipelines, script with Terraform, and learn the cost discipline that keeps a startup's bill survivable. Certification preparation for AWS and Azure associate-level exams runs alongside the build work.

Curriculum: Linux & Networking for Cloud; AWS Core Services; Microsoft Azure Administration; Google Cloud Platform Essentials; Docker & Kubernetes; CI/CD Pipelines & Infrastructure as Code; Cloud Security, Monitoring & Cost Optimisation.
Tools: AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, Docker, Kubernetes, Terraform, GitHub Actions, Linux.
Who it is for: Developers moving into platform engineering; System and network administrators; Graduates targeting high-paying remote roles; Startup engineers owning infrastructure.
Career outcomes (Nigerian salary bands): Cloud Support Engineer ₦400,000 – ₦700,000 / month; DevOps Engineer ₦800,000 – ₦2,000,000 / month; Cloud Architect ₦1,500,000+ / month.

Q: Are cloud lab costs expensive?
A: No. We work inside the free tiers of AWS, Azure and Google Cloud and teach budget alerts, so most learners spend little or nothing on infrastructure during the 14 to 18 week Cloud Computing programme. You learn to set a spending limit on every account before you launch anything on it.

Q: Which cloud should I specialise in?
A: Start with AWS, which has the largest cloud job market, then add Azure, because many Nigerian enterprises are Microsoft-first. The Cloud Computing programme covers AWS, Azure and Google Cloud plus Docker, Kubernetes, Terraform and CI/CD pipelines, so you can move between providers once you know one well.

### Robotics & IoT

Page: https://techfaculty.ng/departments/robotics-iot
Duration: 16-20 weeks. Level: Intermediate to Advanced.
Price: Taken as a Custom Programme: students pick modules from any department, and an order starts at ₦50,000.

Hardware skills are scarce in Nigeria and increasingly valuable as manufacturing, agriculture, energy and security all move toward automation. In this department you wire and programme real devices: microcontrollers, sensors, motors, communication modules and cloud dashboards. You progress from blinking an LED to a working automation project — smart irrigation, energy monitoring or a security system — and learn to run small AI models directly on the device.

Curriculum: Electronics & Circuit Fundamentals; Arduino & Embedded C; Raspberry Pi & Python Control; Sensors, Actuators & Motor Control; IoT Systems Design & Cloud Dashboards; Edge AI on Devices; Capstone Automation Project.
Tools: Arduino, Raspberry Pi, ESP32, Python, C/C++, MQTT, Fusion 360.
Who it is for: Engineering students and technicians; Secondary-school science enthusiasts; Agritech and energy innovators; Makers building physical products.
Career outcomes (Nigerian salary bands): IoT / Embedded Developer ₦400,000 – ₦900,000 / month; Automation Technician ₦250,000 – ₦600,000 / month; Hardware Product Builder Project and contract based.

Q: Do I need to buy my own components?
A: No. Our centres provide shared lab components for classwork, so you can complete the Robotics & IoT programme without buying anything. If you want to keep building at home, starter kits are available at member pricing in the Tech Faculty tech store, which also supplies robotics kits to schools in bulk.

Q: Is programming experience required?
A: No. We teach the C, C++ and Python you need for Arduino, ESP32 and Raspberry Pi boards as part of the 16 to 20 week Robotics & IoT programme. You write code for the circuits and sensors you build in class, so programming is learned alongside the hardware rather than before it.

## Virtual SIWES

Page: https://techfaculty.ng/virtual-siwes
Placement: ₦45,000, paid before onboarding. Includes: Official acceptance and placement letter addressed to your school; Choice of Learn & Pay or Tutor & Earn — the same two tracks we run on site; Weekly live online sessions with a mentor from your department; Real client and product work, not exercises, so your logbook has something to say; Attendance and supervision records kept for your school and the ITF; Completion certificate, recommendation letter and a project portfolio link.
Logbook service: ₦15,000. Includes: We arrange courier pickup of your logbook and ITF forms from your city; Line-by-line review of your weekly entries against the work you actually did; Guidance on documenting your supervised work: we flag thin or unclear entries for you to correct in your own words; Official signing and company stamping by your assigned supervisor; SPE-1, ITF Form 8 and place-of-attachment forms completed where applicable; Return delivery back to you — both legs of the waybill are inside the price. Turnaround: 5–7 working days from the day your logbook reaches our headquarters.

Q: Can I do my SIWES or IT online in Nigeria?
A: Yes. Many institutions accept a remote or hybrid placement for Computer Science, IT, Software Engineering, Data Science and related courses, provided the host is real, registered, relevant and willing to supervise and stamp your logbook. Tech Faculty NG is licensed by the Federal Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation through NBTI. Virtual SIWES costs ₦45,000.

Q: How much does Virtual SIWES cost?
A: The virtual IT placement costs ₦45,000 for the full duration of your training, whether that is three or six months, paid before onboarding. The logbook review, signing, stamping and two-way delivery service is a separate ₦15,000. You can pay online by card, bank transfer or USSD on this page, or reserve your slot and pay by bank transfer when a coordinator sends the details.

Q: Who signs and stamps my SIWES logbook?
A: Your assigned Tech Faculty supervisor signs your logbook, and it is stamped with our official company stamp, exactly as it would be if you sat in our Nnewi office every day. Attendance and supervision records are kept for your school and the ITF throughout your placement, so the signature reflects real supervised work.

Q: How do I send my logbook for review and signing?
A: You do not have to travel. Book the ₦15,000 logbook service and our courier partner collects your logbook and ITF forms from your address in any Nigerian city. We check your entries against your supervision records, complete our company sections of the ITF forms, sign and stamp them, then waybill everything back to you. Both the pickup and the return delivery are included in that price.

Q: How long does the logbook turnaround take?
A: Plan for 5–7 working days from the day your logbook reaches our headquarters, plus courier time each way. If your school's submission deadline is tight, write the date on the form and we prioritise your logbook. Booking the pickup a few weeks before the end of your IT leaves room for corrections before the deadline.

Q: What if my school insists on a physical placement?
A: Then use one of our 22 physical centres instead, including Nnewi, Onitsha, Owerri, Aba, Enugu, Abakaliki and Abuja, with the same tracks and mentors. Some students also do a hybrid: weekly online work with a few on-site weeks. We write your placement letter to match whatever arrangement your school approved.

Q: Which tracks can I do virtually?
A: Both. Learn & Pay is for students who want structured, mentored experience across web development, data analytics, AI, cybersecurity, design or digital marketing. Tutor & Earn is for students already skilled enough to teach: you tutor other learners online, gain teaching experience and earn money while completing your industrial training.

Q: Do I still get a placement letter and completion certificate?
A: Yes. You receive an official acceptance and placement letter addressed to your institution within 48 hours of payment, before you resume. At the end you receive a completion certificate, a recommendation letter and a project portfolio link. Virtual interns are documented exactly like on-site interns, so your school sees the same paperwork.

Q: Will my ITF allowance be affected?
A: No. Your ITF SIWES allowance depends on your school and the ITF processing your SPE-1 and Form 8 correctly and on time, not on whether your placement is remote. We complete our company sections of those ITF forms as part of the logbook service, so nothing stalls on our side.

Q: Can final-year and part-time students use this?
A: Yes. Virtual IT is built for students who cannot relocate: those studying far from our centres, those already working, part-time and sandwich students, and anyone whose approved host fell through late in the session. The same placement letter, weekly mentoring and logbook service apply to every one of them.

Q: What do I need before I start?
A: A laptop where possible, a working internet connection, your school's IT duration and start date, and your logbook and ITF forms once your department issues them. If a laptop is the blocker, ask us: our tech store sells tested student laptops with pay on delivery and part-payment options for exactly this reason.

Q: Is Tech Faculty NG a registered organisation my school can verify?
A: Yes. Tech Faculty NG is a licensed technology training institute, licensed by the Federal Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation through NBTI and headquartered at the Technology Incubation Centre, Nnewi, with centres in 22 Nigerian cities. Your coordinator can verify our licence and address, and our certificates are verifiable online.

Page: https://techfaculty.ng/siwes-success-kit
Everything a Nigerian student needs to land, survive and convert a SIWES placement. Price: ₦4,500.

Q: What exactly do I receive after paying?

Q: Is the free checklist really free?
A: Yes. Enter your email or WhatsApp number and we send the 7-step placement checklist immediately, with no obligation to buy the kit. It covers the same steps our placed students follow, from confirming your course is on the ITF-approved SIWES list to collecting your SPE-1 and ITF Form 8 early.

Q: Does the kit guarantee a placement?
A: No. No honest guide can promise a SIWES placement. The kit gives you the documents, templates and outreach system that our placed students used, but you still have to send the emails and attend the interviews. What it removes is the guesswork about what to send and when.

Prefer to pay by bank transfer to us directly? Reserve your kit and we send the details on WhatsApp or email.

Q: Can I use it if I'm not a Tech Faculty student?
A: Yes. The SIWES Success Kit is written for any Nigerian student on SIWES or industrial training, from any university, polytechnic or college of education. You do not need a Faculty ID or a Tech Faculty placement to use the templates, the checklist or the WhatsApp support channel.

## Side hustles for talent (pay per task)

Page: https://techfaculty.ng/side-hustles
Every business service above is also a paid side hustle. Talent earn ₦5,000 per standard task or ₦10,000 per big task; Testing & QA tasks pay ₦5,000 each (three days of use, then screenshots and a written report). A Tech Faculty manager checks each task and approved tasks are paid weekly, every Friday. Each side hustle has 50 openings, and remote tasks are open nationwide while field work is in covered cities.

How to start:
1. Join the Tech Faculty talent pool (free) and mention this side hustle.
2. Pass a short skills check or sample task.
3. Pick up tasks as businesses order them. Take as many or as few as you can handle.
4. Get paid weekly, every Friday, for every approved task.

## Jobs and talent marketplace

Page: https://techfaculty.ng/careers
One free talent profile is used to apply for Tech Faculty roles and approved client projects. Every saved profile is listed straight away; profile detail improves match ranking. Our system scores suitable roles and the team reviews matches before they are shared. Some roles start with a short work trial before selection, and work after selection is coordinated on Slack.
The board also lists curated remote tech and AI-training jobs (including data annotation, AI writing and evaluation roles) open to Nigerian and African talent, refreshed on the 1st and 15th of each month. Apply directly on the partner platform.

### Partner job platforms

#### Micro1

Page: https://techfaculty.ng/careers/platforms/micro1
Vetted remote engineering roles with US and global companies. Micro1 uses an AI interviewer to vet engineers and experts, then matches them to remote contracts and AI training projects. Pay is typically hourly in USD and depends on skill and seniority.

Q: Is Micro1 legit?
A: Yes. Micro1 is an established AI recruiting company that places vetted talent on remote contracts and AI data projects.

Q: How much does Micro1 pay?
A: Rates vary by role. Engineering and expert roles are usually paid hourly in USD, often well above local market rates.

Q: Can Nigerians apply to Micro1?
A: Yes. Micro1 accepts remote contributors from many countries, including Nigeria. Availability varies by project, so create your account and check which roles are open to your country.

## Software products by Tech Faculty

Page: https://techfaculty.ng/products

### Dear Claire: Anonymous Diary That Replies

Page: https://techfaculty.ng/products/dear-claire
Dear Claire is a free anonymous diary app for Android and iPhone. Write or record a diary entry starting with "Dear Claire" and get a caring reply with real human advice, not AI. It also tracks your mood and lets you help other people anonymously.
Features: Anonymous and private: no real name needed; Real human replies, not a chatbot; Write or record voice diary entries; Mood tracking over time; Read and support other people's anonymous diaries.
Google Play: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.mobymagic.clairediary
App Store: https://apps.apple.com/ng/app/dear-claire-secret-diary-chat/id1635333304

Q: Is Dear Claire free?
A: Yes. Dear Claire is free to download on Google Play and the App Store, with optional in-app purchases.

Q: Are Dear Claire's replies written by AI?
A: No. Replies to your diary entries are written by real people, not a chatbot.

Q: Is Dear Claire anonymous?
A: Yes. You don't need to use your real name, and your diary stays private.

Q: Can I record voice notes instead of typing?
A: Yes. You can type an entry or record it as a voice note.

Q: Is Dear Claire a therapy app?
A: No. It is a supportive diary and not a replacement for professional help. In a crisis, contact your local emergency number.

### Questions asked about every campus

Answers below are for Nnewi; each campus page gives the same answers for its own city and address.

Q: Where exactly is Tech Faculty in Nnewi?
A: Tech Faculty Nnewi operates from Technology Incubation Center, Onitsha-Okigwe Expressway, by Area Command, Umudim, Nnewi, Anambra State, inside the Technology Incubation Centre network of the National Board for Technology Incubation, an agency of the Federal Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation. You train in a federally-run facility rather than a private shopfront, with labs and mentors on site.

Q: Can I study online instead of attending the Nnewi centre?
A: Yes. Every Tech Faculty department can be studied online, hybrid or fully in person. Online study is included in the course fee, hybrid study with monthly meetups adds ₦12,000, and weekly on-site classes add ₦22,500. Many Nnewi students take lectures online and use the centre for labs and project reviews.

Q: Do you accept SIWES and industrial training students in Nnewi?
A: Yes. We take SIWES and IT students each session from institutions such as Nnamdi Azikiwe University, Chukwuemeka Odumegwu Ojukwu University, on our Learn & Pay and Tutor & Earn tracks. There is no separate placement fee on site, and SIWES students can get up to 50% off Learn & Pay course fees. Virtual SIWES costs ₦45,000, and our ₦15,000 logbook service completes the company sections of your ITF SPE-1 and Form 8 if you cannot attend in person.

Q: Are there holiday tech programmes for children and teenagers in Nnewi?
A: Yes. During school holidays we run teen tracks in Digital Creation, Coding, Artificial Intelligence and Cybersecurity for JSS and SSS students in Nnewi. Classes are project-based and supervised, each student ends by presenting what they built, and fees start from ₦45,000 for a 4-week track.
